AI has uncovered hidden patterns in the progression of COPD, supporting a shift from reactive to anticipatory management. Translation to routine care requires prospective validation, improved interpretability, workflow integration, and generalizability and equity.

records.title: A bibliometric analysis and visualization of trends in cervical cancer screening technologies based on dual-database analysis.

content.title: A bibliometric analysis and visualization of trends in cervical cancer screening technologies based on dual-database analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Cervical cancer is a leading cause of gynecologic cancer mortality, especially in low- and middle-income countries. Early detection through screening is essential to reduce incidence and death rates. Advances in high-risk HPV molecular assays, liquid-based cytology (LBC), and AI-assisted diagnostics have transformed screening strategies. However, a systematic, quantitative assessment remains lacking. This study uses cross-database validation and bibliometrics to explore cervical cancer screening trends. It provides insights for clinical practice and future research.

Methodology

This study is a bibliometric analysis rather than a traditional systematic review. We searched Web of Science and PubMed for cervical cancer screening articles from 2000 to 2024. Criteria included clinical trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, observational studies, and animal experiments. Conference abstracts and non-academic publications were excluded. After deduplication using CiteSpace, 640 unique articles from PubMed were cross-validated with WoSCC data. We used VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and R for data analysis. Co-occurrence and cluster analysis identified research trends. This bibliometric analysis was reported in accordance with the BIBLIO checklist and informed, where applicable, by the GLOBAL guidance for reporting bibliometric analyses.

Objectives

The study analyzes research trends in cervical cancer screening using Web of Science and PubMed. It identifies high-frequency keywords, research collaboration networks, technological advances, and geographical patterns. Findings highlight global focus on HPV, cytology, and AI. These trends help guide scientific policy and clinical practices.

Results

The study includes 1,160 articles from 2000 to 2024, showing a steady increase in publications. The US, China, and India lead in research output. Philip E. Castle is the most prolific author, and Harvard University has the highest citation rate. Core topics include "cervical cancer," "HPV," and "screening." Emerging trends involve "positive women," "impact," and "AI." This signals a shift toward precise and automated screening.

Conclusion

The study demonstrates increased academic interest in cervical cancer screening technologies from 2000 to 2024. Research has focused on advancing screening methods, early detection, and effective program implementation. Future efforts should prioritize detection accuracy and enhance accessibility in low-resource settings. We must also standardize clinical protocols for cervical cancer prevention.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence for Opioid Safety Surveillance from Clinical Text: A Clinically Focused Review.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence for Opioid Safety Surveillance from Clinical Text: A Clinically Focused Review.
content.abstract: Opioid-related iatrogenic harms, including opioid use disorder, overdose, and opioid-induced respiratory depression, constitute a major patient safety challenge. Although clinicians document key safety signals in unstructured clinical narratives, many of these indicators are not readily captured by conventional surveillance approaches that rely on structured administrative data. This clinically focused narrative review synthesizes 47 empirical studies published between 2009 and 2025 that applied artificial intelligence (AI) methods to identify opioid-related harms from clinical text and to address the resulting ascertainment gap. Across studies, administrative coding systems, including ICD-10, often under-ascertain opioid-related events, whereas text-based AI can identify additional cases and contextual details often documented primarily in narrative records, such as fluctuating mental status, suspected drug causality, and responses to naloxone. Methodologically, the literature has progressed from interpretable rule-based lexicons to machine learning and deep learning models and, more recently, to transformer-based approaches, including large language models (LLMs) for classification and schema-driven extraction. Rule-based systems established the feasibility of transparent surveillance and frequently recovered clinically documented cases missed by billing codes. Subsequent supervised and deep learning approaches expanded scalability and, in a smaller subset of studies, were integrated into electronic health record workflows with operational metrics reported. More recent transformer- and LLM-based studies emphasize richer extraction schemas and benchmark development, including characterization of overdose context and intentionality and identification of potential prodromal neurocognitive signals, although external validation, calibration, and prospective outcome evaluation remain inconsistently reported. Given that the evidence base is predominantly retrospective and that clinical workflow studies remain comparatively few, a pragmatic near-term clinical role is to provide detection-to-triage decision support rather than autonomous diagnosis, in which systems surface candidate cases with reviewable evidence for clinician adjudication. Future progress will require greater standardization of phenotype definitions, routine equity auditing and subgroup reporting, stronger external validation and calibration at operational thresholds, and a shift from retrospective discrimination metrics toward prospective assessments of the clinical workflow impact, clinical utility, and patient-centered outcomes.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence for Classification of Endoscopic Severity of Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Systematic Review and Critical Appraisal.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence for Classification of Endoscopic Severity of Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Systematic Review and Critical Appraisal.
content.abstract:
Background

Endoscopic scoring indices for ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease are subject to inter-endoscopist variability. There is increasing interest in the development of deep learning models to standardize endoscopic assessment of intestinal diseases. Here, we summarize and critically appraise the literature on artificial intelligence-assisted endoscopic characterization of inflammatory bowel disease severity.

Methods

A systematic search of Ovid MEDLINE, EMBASE, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and IEEE Xplore was performed to identify reports of AI systems used for endoscopic severity classification of IBD. Selected studies were critically appraised for methodological and reporting quality using APPRAISE-AI.

Results

Thirty-one studies published between 2019 and 2024 were included. Of 31 studies, 28 studies examined endoscopic classification of ulcerative colitis and 3 examined Crohn's disease. Researchers sought to accomplish a wide range of classification tasks, including binary and multilevel classification, based on still images or full-length colonoscopy videos. Overall scores for study quality ranged from 41 (moderate quality) to 64 (high quality) out of 100, with 28 out of 31 studies within the moderate quality range. The highest-scoring domains were clinical relevance and reporting quality, while the lowest-scoring domains were robustness of results and reproducibility.

Conclusions

Multiple AI models have demonstrated the potential for clinical translation for ulcerative colitis. Research concerning the endoscopic severity assessment of Crohn's disease is limited and should be further explored. More rigorous external validation of AI models and increased transparency of data and codes are needed to improve the quality of AI studies.

records.title: Application Progress of Machine Learning in Prognostic Prediction of Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review.

content.title: Application Progress of Machine Learning in Prognostic Prediction of Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review.
content.abstract: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) has become a cornerstone treatment for coronary artery disease; however, accurate prognostic prediction remains a significant clinical challenge. Machine learning technologies demonstrate tremendous potential in PCI prognostic prediction by analyzing vast amounts of clinical data and identifying complex nonlinear relationships among variables. This article systematically reviews recent advances in machine learning applications for PCI prognostic prediction, encompassing predictive targets including in-hospital mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events, bleeding complications, and long-term survival. Algorithms such as random forest, support vector machines, neural networks, and deep learning have demonstrated superior predictive performance compared to traditional risk scoring systems across multiple studies. Deep learning approaches exhibit particular advantages in processing multimodal data. Nevertheless, significant challenges remain regarding model interpretability, external validation, and clinical implementation. Future research should prioritize the development of explainable artificial intelligence systems, the conduct of multicenter validation studies, and the establishment of regulatory frameworks for clinical deployment.

records.title: Diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence assisted clinical imaging in the detection of oral potentially malignant disorders and oral cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence assisted clinical imaging in the detection of oral potentially malignant disorders and oral cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

The objective of this study is to examine the application of artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms in detecting oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMD) and oral cancerous lesions, and to evaluate the accuracy variations among different imaging tools employed in these diagnostic processes.

Materials and methods

A systematic search was conducted in four databases: Embase, Web of Science, PubMed, and Scopus. The inclusion criteria included studies using machine learning algorithms to provide diagnostic information on specific oral lesions, prospective or retrospective design, and inclusion of OPMD. Sensitivity and specificity analyses were also required. Forest plots were generated to display overall diagnostic odds ratio (DOR), sensitivity, specificity, negative predictive values, and summary receiver operating characteristic (SROC) curves. Meta-regression analysis was conducted to examine potential differences among different imaging tools.

Results

The overall DOR for AI-based screening of OPMD and oral mucosal cancerous lesions from normal mucosa was 68.438 (95% CI= [39.484-118.623], I2 =86%). The area under the SROC curve was 0.938, indicating excellent diagnostic performance. AI-assisted screening showed a sensitivity of 89.9% (95% CI= [0.866-0.925]; I2 =81%), specificity of 89.2% (95% CI= [0.851-0.922], I2 =79%), and a high negative predictive value of 89.5% (95% CI= [0.851-0.927], I2 =96%). Meta-regression analysis revealed no significant difference among the three image tools. After generating a GOSH plot, the DOR was calculated to be 49.30, and the area under the SROC curve was 0.877. Additionally, sensitivity, specificity, and negative predictive value were 90.5% (95% CI [0.873-0.929], I2 =4%), 87.0% (95% CI [0.813-0.912], I2 =49%) and 90.1% (95% CI [0.860-0.931], I2 =57%), respectively. Subgroup analysis showed that clinical photography had the highest diagnostic accuracy.

Conclusions

AI-based detection using clinical photography shows a high DOR and is easily accessible in the current era with billions of phone subscribers globally. This indicates that there is significant potential for AI to enhance the diagnostic capabilities of general practitioners to the level of specialists by utilizing clinical photographs, without the need for expensive specialized imaging equipment.

records.title: Hypertensive disorders in pregnancy and risk of asthma in the offspring: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Hypertensive disorders in pregnancy and risk of asthma in the offspring: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), including preeclampsia, gestational hypertension, and eclampsia, are common pregnancy complications that may have long-term consequences for offspring health. Emerging evidence suggests a potential link between maternal hypertension and childhood asthma, though findings remain inconsistent. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to synthesize the existing evidence on the association between HDP and asthma risk in offspring.

Methods

A comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and EMBASE was conducted from database inception to 3 December 2024, restricted to peer-reviewed published studies. The eligibility criteria followed the PICOS framework. Observational studies (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional) assessing the association between HDP and asthma in offspring were included. Effect measures were converted to odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI), and a meta-analysis was performed using random- and fixed-effects models. Heterogeneity was assessed jointly with Cochran's Q test (p < 0.10) and the I 2 statistic, and publication bias was examined through funnel plots and Egger's test.

Results

Twenty studies encompassing over three million mother-infant pairs were included. The pooled OR for asthma risk in offspring of mothers with HDP was 1.14 (95% CI: 1.07-1.21), indicating a significant association. Subgroup analyses revealed a positive association with both preeclampsia (OR: 1.20; 95% CI: 1.12-1.28) and gestational hypertension (OR: 1.18; 95% CI: 1.02-1.36). Heterogeneity was high in some subgroups, such as gestational hypertension (I 2 = 92.6%; p < 0.0001), suggesting variability across studies. As a secondary outcome, the association between HDP and wheezing in the offspring was assessed. The pooled OR was 1.07 (95% CI: 0.99-1.17), not reaching statistical significance, although positive trends were observed in some subtypes.

Conclusion

Maternal HDP is associated with an approximately 14-20% increased risk of asthma in offspring, highlighting the need for targeted early-life monitoring and intervention strategies. Further research is warranted to elucidate underlying mechanisms and optimize maternal-fetal health outcomes.

Systematic review registration

IS: CRD420251000229.

records.title: Digital Dentistry and Artificial Intelligence: A Systematic Review on Innovations in Diagnosis, Treatment Planning, and Prosthodontics.

content.title: Digital Dentistry and Artificial Intelligence: A Systematic Review on Innovations in Diagnosis, Treatment Planning, and Prosthodontics.
content.abstract: Digital dentistry has rapidly evolved through the integration of advanced imaging, computer-aided design (CAD) and manufacturing (CAM), and data-driven workflows, creating opportunities for artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled clinical support across multiple dental domains. Although numerous studies have explored AI in isolated diagnostic or restorative applications, a comprehensive synthesis spanning diagnosis, treatment planning, and prosthodontics remains limited, leaving uncertainty regarding the overall scope and maturity of current evidence. This systematic review aimed to consolidate and evaluate published research on AI applications within digital dentistry, with emphasis on data modalities, algorithmic tasks, and reported clinical outcomes. A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-compliant search was conducted across PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2015 and 2025. Eligible peer-reviewed studies reporting quantitative outcomes were systematically screened, extracted, and synthesized descriptively. The review identified a predominance of image-based diagnostic applications, particularly for caries detection and anatomical segmentation, with fewer studies addressing treatment planning and prosthodontic workflows. Deep learning models were most frequently employed, and reported outcomes commonly focused on accuracy, segmentation performance, and spatial agreement. The findings indicate that AI is increasingly embedded within digital dental workflows, primarily as a decision support tool rather than a standalone system. This synthesis clarifies current research trends, highlights the relative maturity of diagnostic applications, and underscores the expanding but uneven integration of artificial intelligence across interconnected stages of digital dentistry, providing a consolidated evidence base to inform clinicians and researchers.

records.title: Research Fronts 2025: Mapping the evolving landscape of global science and technology.

content.title: Research Fronts 2025: Mapping the evolving landscape of global science and technology.
content.abstract: This study employs co-citation analysis of highly cited core papers, complemented by expert interpretation, to identify 128 hot and emerging research fronts for 2025 across 11 broad areas of natural and social sciences. By combining a macroscopic overview with microscopic examinations, the study characterizes the developmental momentum of each area and conducts in-depth interpretations of selected key fronts to elucidate their strategic value and scientific breakthroughs. Prominent themes garnering significant attention include the planetary boundaries framework, high-throughput single-cell technologies, high-temperature polymer dielectrics, petawatt-class lasers, dark matter detection, etc. Furthermore, organized basic research utilizing large-scale infrastructure and deep interdisciplinary integration is actively expanding the boundaries of human knowledge. Crucially, the findings demonstrate a flourishing scientific revolution characterized by the rapid emergence of new theories and technologies. The analysis highlights a profound paradigm shift in which artificial intelligence (AI) transcends its role as a mere tool to become the core engine reshaping research across mathematics, life sciences, and social sciences. Ultimately, by illuminating these specific focal points, this study serves as a vital resource for researchers and policymakers to monitor the evolving trajectory of basic science and future development trends.

records.title: Identification of metabolic vulnerabilities and synthetic lethal targets utilizing artificial intelligence-driven precision medicine.

content.title: Identification of metabolic vulnerabilities and synthetic lethal targets utilizing artificial intelligence-driven precision medicine.
content.abstract: Cancer metabolism is highly plastic, and most attempts to turn that plasticity into a therapeutic target fail for a specific, recurring reason: a computational prediction of a metabolic vulnerability is not the same evidentiary object as an experimentally confirmed one, and the two are routinely discussed as if they were interchangeable. This review takes that distinction as its starting point rather than its conclusion. Artificial intelligence and genome-scale systems biology have made it easy to generate metabolic hypotheses at a scale no experimental program could match - machine learning models trained on genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data now output candidate vulnerabilities, biomarkers, and drug combinations faster than they can be tested - but the resulting literature has not been consistently honest about how far any given prediction has actually traveled toward clinical relevance. We examine six areas where this gap is most visible: multi-omics data integration, genome-scale metabolic network modeling, computational discovery of metabolic vulnerabilities and synthetic lethal interactions, single-cell and spatial resolution of metabolic heterogeneity, AI-guided drug and biomarker discovery, and the small set of studies that have actually reached clinical testing. Rather than summarizing these areas as separate literatures, we grade every substantive finding discussed against an explicit four-tier evidence standard - associative, mechanistic, perturbation-validated, or clinically tested - and we apply that standard critically rather than deferentially: several widely cited computational vulnerabilities remain unconfirmed outside the cell lines in which they were discovered, genome-scale models continue to carry unresolved gaps in reaction coverage that limit their predictive reach, and, of the AI-derived metabolic predictions discussed in this review, only one has so far been tested in a completed prospective clinical trial. We argue that this shortage of prospective validation, not a shortage of computational sophistication, is the field's central constraint, and we close by identifying where methodological effort would do the most good: standardized validation reporting, tissue-resolved rather than bulk metabolic models, and closer coupling between computational prediction and the specific experimental designs capable of falsifying it.

records.title: Operationalising digital and AI pathology in translational research and drug development: an infrastructure and regulatory perspective from biobank to companion diagnostic.

content.title: Operationalising digital and AI pathology in translational research and drug development: an infrastructure and regulatory perspective from biobank to companion diagnostic.
content.abstract: Digital and artificial intelligence (AI) pathology have advanced rapidly and are increasingly embedded in translational research, clinical trials and regulated diagnostic devices. Multiple reviews have addressed the underlying computational methods, oncology applications and clinical translation barriers; however, the operational and regulatory infrastructure required to deploy these technologies across the full drug-development pipeline remains under-reviewed. This structured narrative review synthesises peer-reviewed literature and regulatory documents identified through searches of PubMed, Embase and Web of Science between January 2019 and April 2026 (78 sources retained) on the end-to-end ecosystem connecting AI-ready tissue biobanks, preclinical pathology, AI-assisted patient screening, clinical-trial endpoint adjudication, central pathology review, Contract Research Organization (CRO) workflows and US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulatory pathways governing In Vitro Diagnostics (IVD), Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) and Companion Diagnostics (CDx). Unlike prior method-centric or oncology-clinician-centric reviews, we focus on the infrastructure between models and patients, including Laboratory Information Systems (LIS), Image Management Systems (IMS), AI orchestration and structured reporting under Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments, College of American Pathologists, Good Laboratory Practice, Good Clinical Laboratory Practice, Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act and FDA frameworks. We provide a vendor-agnostic comparison of integrated pathology platforms, a mapping of FDA regulatory pathways (510(k), De Novo, premarket approval) to digital-pathology product categories, a stage-by-stage map from each drug-development challenge to its enabling infrastructure and regulatory framework, and a critical appraisal of the unresolved bottlenecks that gate broad adoption: domain shift, interpretability, annotation cost, algorithmic bias, external validation, regulatory uncertainty and reimbursement. A governed, interoperable LIS, IMS and AI ecosystem is a prerequisite for translating digital-pathology research into regulator-grade evidence. Priorities include external validation against reporting standards (Transparent Reporting of a multivariable prediction model for Individual Prognosis or Diagnosis - Artificial Intelligence (TRIPOD-AI), Checklist for Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging (CLAIM), Development and Early-stage Clinical Identification and Delegation Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence (DECIDE-AI)), harmonisation with the EU AI Act and EU Medical Device Regulation and cost-effectiveness evaluation in real-world deployment.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in emergency trauma perioperative management: applications, performance benchmarks, and translation barriers.

content.title: Artificial intelligence in emergency trauma perioperative management: applications, performance benchmarks, and translation barriers.
content.abstract: This review examines the current status of artificial intelligence (AI) applications in the perioperative management of emergency trauma. Published studies suggest performance advantages of AI over traditional methods in prehospital triage, radiographic injury detection, massive transfusion prediction, and early warning of postoperative complications, although findings vary across study designs and validation settings. However, actual adoption in trauma care remains limited due to data heterogeneity, performance degradation in external validation, workflow integration challenges, lack of interpretability, and a scarcity of prospective interventional evidence. This review further argues that methodologically inflated benchmark performance constitutes an underrecognized barrier to adoption in its own right, and that bridging the implementation gap will likely require a shift from area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC)-centered reporting toward reporting sensitivity at prespecified clinical thresholds and evaluating patient outcomes in prospective interventional trials.

records.title: A Case-Based Framework for Teaching Artificial Intelligence Applications in Medical Education.
records.publisher: MedEdPORTAL : the journal of teaching and learning resources

content.title: A Case-Based Framework for Teaching Artificial Intelligence Applications in Medical Education.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML)-based tools are emerging across many areas of medicine. The next generation of medical professionals must be prepared to critically assess the tools they will use, including how they work and the ethical or legal implications of their implementation. To address this need, we developed a generalizable case-writing framework that enables educators and learners to engage with clinical cases integrating AI/ML concepts, clinical reasoning, and ethical considerations.

Methods

We designed a case-writing template to compose clinical case scenarios that integrate clinical, technical, and ethical/legal learning objectives relating to AI applications in medicine. Medical students used this template to construct 3 cases. Student-authored cases were presented to a broader audience in 1-hour sessions: first as a pilot event, then as a class-wide lecture for 140 fourth-year medical students in a transition-into-residency course.

Results

After the sessions, student audiences had a statistically significant increase in familiarity with key AI terminology, a greater appreciation for the importance of ethical considerations of AI applications in health care, and an increased perceived importance of integrating AI-related topics into the medical curriculum.

Discussion

A case-based framework provides a scalable approach to integrating AI education into existing curricula by connecting clinical scenarios with technical concepts and the ethical considerations of AI adoption; cases offer a familiar format that helps learners understand AI applications in patient care while exploring implementation challenges. The case-writing template and 3 sample cases are provided as adaptable resources for educators seeking to incorporate AI literacy.

records.title: Modeling distinct pathogenesis of early- and late-onset preeclampsia via hierarchical representation learning of interactome.

content.title: Modeling distinct pathogenesis of early- and late-onset preeclampsia via hierarchical representation learning of interactome.
content.abstract:
Objectives

We developed and validated the pathogenesis models by hierarchical representation learning of interactomes connecting endometrial maturation, placentation, chorioamnionitis, and hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme, and low platelet (HELLP) syndrome.

Methods

We utilized 19 gene sets from our previous work to infer interactomes to develop (n = 177) and validate (n = 352) explainable artificial intelligence models for each preeclampsia subtype using deep-insight visible neural network, gradient-weighted class activation mapping, and large language model.

Results

The hierarchically learned representations identified novel genes for late-onset preeclampsia (LOPE), similar to chorioamnionitis (ANKRD13A, SLA), and HELLP syndrome (PDE5A). We also identified novel genes for early-onset preeclampsia (EOPE), similar to HELLP syndrome (SWAP70, GREM2, GPR146, PIP5K1B, EZR).

Conclusions

Our pathogenesis models connected HELLP syndrome with both LOPE and EOPE. However, chorioamnionitis was only connected with LOPE.

records.title: A Review of Mechanistic and Hybrid Artificial Intelligence Models for Predicting Pesticide Fate and Transport in Soil and Water

content.title: A Review of Mechanistic and Hybrid Artificial Intelligence Models for Predicting Pesticide Fate and Transport in Soil and Water
content.abstract: Global pesticide use exceeded 3.7 million tonnes in 2023, and residues that persist beyond the treated field drive diffuse soil, surface water, and groundwater contamination linked to ecological harm and an estimated 150,000 pesticide poisoning deaths annually. Because field monitoring of pesticide fate across every soil, climate, and hydrological setting is logistically and financially infeasible at regulatory scale, predictive modelling has become the primary tool for estimating environmental concentrations and associated risk. This review traces the development of the field from traditional process-based mechanisms to hybrid AI frameworks by synthesizing 81 peer-reviewed and technical sources from an initial pool of 1,450 records screened across Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect (2005–2026). We look at the physicochemical and degradation principles that determine the fate of pesticides; the deterministic, mechanistic, process-based, empirical, and statistical models that support the current regulatory risk assessment; the hydrological and transport models that function at the soil profile to watershed scale; and the expanding array of machine learning, deep learning, fuzzy logic, GIS, remote sensing, and IoT-enabled techniques that are transforming precision agriculture and prediction. Case studies from India and other countries demonstrate real-world uses in addition to ongoing limitations in data accessibility and cross-context transferability. We point out important gaps, such as persistent data scarcity in low- and middle-income regions, limited coupling of fate models to downscaled climate projections, and inadequate integration of explainable AI to foster regulatory trust. We identify calibration and validation, particularly probabilistic uncertainty quantification, as essential to the responsible use of both conventional and data-driven models. We conclude that creating accurate, transferable pesticide prediction systems that support the Sustainable Development Goals and safeguard human and environmental health requires combining mechanistic understanding with hybrid, physics-informed AI and climate-resilient precision agriculture technologies.

records.title: Beyond Accuracy: Validation, Reproducibility, and Deployment Readiness of AI in Food Safety and Quality.

content.title: Beyond Accuracy: Validation, Reproducibility, and Deployment Readiness of AI in Food Safety and Quality.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly proposed for detecting microbial and chemical hazards in food, but laboratory accuracies are rarely reproduced in routine use. This structured narrative review examined whether reported performance is traceable, independently validated, and transferable to operational settings. Eight bibliographic databases and seven institutional routes were searched for English-language records published from January 2018 to May 2026, and we screened the records; the final corpus comprised 76 sources (53 journal articles, 9 conference papers, 2 preprints, and 12 institutional or regulatory documents). Seven primary studies supporting the quantitative evidence were appraised individually against 11 indicators, including test-set independence, external validation, and leakage control. Physical-hazard inspection and narrow-matrix spectral grading had the strongest deployment evidence, whereas microbial and chemical screening remained at laboratory or pilot scale. Among the appraised studies, the most credible estimates came from physically or temporally independent test sets, and no sensor-based study evaluated transfer to another instrument or laboratory. Deep learning showed clear advantages for image-based tasks but not consistently for small-sample spectral calibration. Adoption is limited mainly by validation design, recalibration burden, false-alarm costs, and the absence of a regulatory pathway rather than by accuracy. AI is best positioned as a screening and decision-support layer linked to confirmatory testing and human oversight.

records.title: Application of artificial intelligence in predicting periodontal risks in orthodontic patients: a scoping review.

content.title: Application of artificial intelligence in predicting periodontal risks in orthodontic patients: a scoping review.
content.abstract:
Introduction

This scoping review aims to evaluate artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning, for predicting periodontal risks in orthodontic patients and to identify methodological gaps limiting clinical translation.

Methods

Reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR and PRISMA-S guidelines, a systematic search was conducted across six electronic databases (PubMed, IEEE Xplore, Web of Science, Scopus, Embase, Cochrane Library), grey literature, and citation tracking (Jan 1, 2018-June 1, 2025). Out of 880 identified records (312 duplicates removed; 568 screened), 56 full texts were evaluated, yielding 3 core clinical CBCT studies meeting strict eligibility criteria (Xu et al., 2024; Pirayesh et al., 2024; Zheng et al., 2025). Methodological quality and risk of bias were appraised using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST.

Results

Reported performance for orthodontically induced inflammatory root resorption (OIIRR) ranged from 82.1% accuracy in small canine-induced resorption cohorts to >94% accuracy in larger grading frameworks. However, critical appraisal revealed a high risk of bias across all studies due to single-center retrospective designs, lack of independent external validation, and missing calibration metrics. Direct clinical evidence for AI prediction of gingival recession or orthodontic alveolar bone loss was insufficient within strict pre-cutoff parameters.

Discussion

While AI demonstrates technical feasibility for assessing orthodontically related root resorption risk, robust individual-level risk prediction remains unestablished. Prospective multicenter external validation and adherence to standardized reporting guidelines are required prior to routine clinical adoption.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Chronic Coronary Syndromes: Linking Cellular Pathways to Precision Risk Prediction.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Chronic Coronary Syndromes: Linking Cellular Pathways to Precision Risk Prediction.
content.abstract: Chronic coronary syndromes (CCSs) are no longer defined only by fixed stenosis of the epicardial coronary arteries. CCSs reflect a dynamic biological process. Key contributors include endothelial activation, lipid retention, macrophage foam-cell formation, vascular smooth muscle cell phenotypic switching, and extracellular matrix remodelling. Microvascular rarefaction, perivascular adipose tissue inflammation, cardiometabolic comorbidity, and biological ageing add further complexity. This broader cellular and molecular model provides a rationale for artificial intelligence (AI), because conventional tools often assess anatomy, physiology, inflammation, and systemic biology in isolation. In this narrative review, we examine how AI and machine learning may support a more mechanistic and individualised approach to CCS by linking cellular pathways to measurable clinical signatures. We focus on AI-enabled plaque phenotyping, non-invasive physiology and ischaemia modelling, assessment of coronary microvascular dysfunction, perivascular inflammation mapping, and the integration of multi-omics with cardiometabolic risk profiling. Most of these tools, however, provide imaging-based or data-derived surrogates rather than direct measurements of endothelial activation, inflammation, or calcification biology. Within this limitation, current evidence suggests that AI can quantify subvisual high-risk plaque features, support non-invasive flow assessment, detect imaging patterns associated with microvascular dysfunction and perivascular inflammation, and, in research settings, relate molecular signatures to long-term cardiovascular risk. Clinical adoption remains constrained by retrospective study designs, limited external validation, heterogeneous imaging protocols, gaps in explainability, regulatory uncertainty, and algorithmic bias across sex, ethnicity, age, and resource settings. Future work should prioritise prospective trials, transparent reporting, federated validation, clinically interpretable outputs, and integration with guideline-based decision pathways. The greatest value of AI in CCS is likely to lie in augmenting mechanistic risk stratification and enabling precision prevention for patients whose risk is poorly captured by anatomy alone.

records.title: The Application of Artificial Intelligence in Brucellosis: Diagnosis, Genomic Analysis, Epidemiological Prediction and Drug Discovery.
records.publisher: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

content.title: The Application of Artificial Intelligence in Brucellosis: Diagnosis, Genomic Analysis, Epidemiological Prediction and Drug Discovery.
content.abstract: Brucellosis, a globally significant zoonosis caused by Brucella, poses a substantial impediment to the sustainable development of the livestock industry and threatens public health security. Traditional control and prevention strategies for brucellosis suffer from fundamental limitations. These include the time-consuming, biosafety risks associated with bacterial culture and the difficulty in differentiating between natural infection and vaccine-induced immunity with serological tests. There remains a challenge in accurately distinguishing vaccine strains from wild-type strains via genotyping methods. Furthermore, current practice relies on manual reporting and empirical judgment without real-time data support. Consequently, these challenges could hinder early detection and reduce the efficiency of large-scale screening, which leads to imprecise outbreak tracing and fails to meet the practical demands of modern livestock production for rapid diagnosis, intelligent prevention and control. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) technologies have been widely applied in the field of veterinary microbiology, which could offer novel technical pathways for the prevention and control of brucellosis. This paper reviews the latest research progress in the application of AI for the rapid diagnosis of brucellosis, genomic analysis and antimicrobial resistance prediction of Brucella, epidemiological risk early warning and the development of drugs and vaccines. We further analyze the current limitations of AI in brucellosis research including the scarcity of high-quality, annotated datasets, insufficient model interpretability and low efficiency in on-site translation and implementation. The paper provides an outlook on the future development of AI-based intelligent prevention and control systems for brucellosis, which offer a theoretical reference and innovative perspectives for the fundamental research and clinical application of AI technologies. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first review to integrate AI applications across the entire chain of brucellosis prevention and control and to propose a conceptual framework for AI-driven intelligent brucellosis management.

records.title: Agentic AI and related systems in nursing and nursing-adjacent work: a scoping review of task allocation, decision authority, and accountability.

content.title: Agentic AI and related systems in nursing and nursing-adjacent work: a scoping review of task allocation, decision authority, and accountability.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) and related systems are being investigated for nursing and nursing-adjacent work, but inconsistent terminology and heterogeneous evaluations obscure their operational capabilities and clinical relevance. This review examined the relationship between reported agentic behavior, evaluation in nursing practice, retained decision authority, and evidence concerning patient benefit, workload, and accountability.

Methods

We conducted a scoping review informed by JBI guidance and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR. We searched PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Scopus, and Web of Science, supplemented by citation and linked-report searching.

Results

Among 28 reports, 13 satisfied all criteria, four were indeterminate, and 11 lacked at least one criterion. Only two qualifying reports evaluated live nurse-AI workflows. Nursing participation ranged from clinical work to education, co-design, output rating, and outcome assessment, and did not uniformly represent runtime control. Patient-facing clinical workflows retained professional decision authority; robotics evaluations involved neither nurses nor patients. Outcomes principally concerned technical performance, communication, usability, or component-specific efficiency. The evidence did not establish autonomous nursing practice, sustained patient benefit, or reduced complete-episode nursing workload. No empirical evaluation of accountability or redress following AI-related error was identified.

Discussion

Operational qualification, clinical benefit, and accountable use require separate evaluation. Future studies should assess the complete human-AI pathway, including verification, correction, escalation, patient outcomes, and responses to failure. Comparative designs should isolate agentic mechanisms from additional computation, information access, and workflow redesign. A proposed post hoc, unvalidated heuristic links allocated function, decision authority, assurance, and accountability/redress. Interpretation is limited by absent prospective registration, unquantified agreement before consensus, related reports, and the absence of formal risk-of-bias assessment.

Conclusion

Agentic capability alone does not establish clinical readiness. Expanding AI-enabled functions requires evidence of meaningful benefit, effective human control, and accountability arrangements proportionate to the consequences of system actions.

records.title: Factors associated with cancer-related fatigue in breast cancer patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Factors associated with cancer-related fatigue in breast cancer patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Cancer-related fatigue (CRF) remains one of the most common and persistent complications among breast cancer survivors, profoundly impairing their psychosocial well-being. Although various predictors have been proposed, existing evidence yields inconsistent findings. This study aimed to systematically synthesize multidimensional factors associated with CRF in this population, providing an evidence-based framework for identifying the individuals and tailoring early interventions.

Methods

A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library and Web of Science databases for studies investigating factors associated with fatigue in breast cancer patients, The search covered the period from database inception to May 3, 2026. Two researchers independently performed study screening, quality assessment, and data extraction, and statistical analyses were performed using Stata 19.0.

Results

16 studies involving a total of 11,984 patients were included. Some potentially relevant factors were identified: pain (OR 1.78, 95% CI 1.29-2.45), dyspnea (OR 2.01, 95% CI 1.10-3.66), anxiety (OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.12-1.86), depression (OR 1.97, 95% CI 1.49-2.60), sleep disturbances (OR 2.02, 95% CI 1.05-3.87) and BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2 (OR 1.36, 95% CI 1.05-1.75).

Conclusion

The patients with cancer- related fatigue in breast cancer, pain, dyspnea, anxiety, depression, sleep disturbances (OR 2.02, 95% CI 1.05-3.87) and BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2 may be associated with fatigue and should be considered as potential related factors.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261432176.

records.title: AI-empowered human microbiome research.

content.title: AI-empowered human microbiome research.
content.abstract: Recent advances in high-throughput microbiome profiling have generated expansive data sets that offer unprecedented opportunities to investigate the role of microbes in human health. However, the complexity and high dimensionality of these data present significant analytical challenges that often exceed the capabilities of traditional computational methods. Artificial intelligence (AI), encompassing both classical machine learning and modern deep learning approaches, has emerged as a powerful solution to these challenges. In this review, we systematically explore AI-driven methodologies in microbiome research, including clustering algorithms, dimensionality reduction techniques, convolutional and recurrent neural networks, and emerging large language models. We assess how these approaches enable the extraction of meaningful biological patterns from complex microbial data from a multiscale perspective, facilitating insights into community dynamics, host-microbe interactions and functional genomics. Additionally, we explore the transformative impact of AI on translational applications across both academic research and real-world clinical settings, including disease diagnostics, therapeutic development and precision microbiome engineering. By critically evaluating the current capabilities and limitations of AI in this context, this review aims to chart a path forward for the integration of AI into microbiome research, ultimately accelerating innovations in personalised medicine and deepening our understanding of host-microbiome relationships.

records.title: Meta-analysis of the effect of nafamostat mesilate versus no-anticoagulation regimens in adult patients undergoing continuous renal replacement therapy.

content.title: Meta-analysis of the effect of nafamostat mesilate versus no-anticoagulation regimens in adult patients undergoing continuous renal replacement therapy.
content.abstract:
Background

Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is a critical treatment for critically ill patients with acute kidney injury. However, effective anticoagulation of the extracorporeal circuit remains a clinical challenge. Nafamostat mesilate (NM), a serine protease inhibitor, possesses localized anticoagulation properties; however, its efficacy and safety in high-bleeding-risk populations have not been systematically evaluated.

Objective

To compare the efficacy and safety of NM anticoagulation and no-anticoagulation regimens in patients undergoing CRRT.

Methods

Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and cohort studies were retrieved from PubMed, Web of Science, MEDLINE, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature, the Cochrane Library, Wanfang Database, Chinese National Knowledge Infrastructure, and the Chinese Biomedical Literature Database. We included studies on adult patients receiving CRRT where the intervention and control groups were treated with NM anticoagulation and no-anticoagulation regimens, respectively. Primary outcomes included filter lifespan, number of filters used, coagulation indicators, bleeding events, and in-hospital mortality. The meta-analysis was conducted using RevMan 5.4 software.

Results

Eight studies involving 969 patients were included. The meta-analysis demonstrated that, compared with the control group, the NM group had a significantly prolonged filter lifespan (P = 0.01) and a reduced number of filters used (P < 0.0001). The activated partial thromboplastin time (P = 0.89), prothrombin time (P = 0.88), and international normalized ratio (P = 0.60) showed no significant differences. Both groups demonstrated clinically similar risks of bleeding events (P = 0.53). However, the NM group demonstrated a significantly reduced in-hospital mortality, compared with the control group (P = 0.02).

Conclusion

The NM anticoagulation regimen effectively extended the CRRT filter lifespan, reduced resource consumption, and improved patient survival outcomes without increasing the bleeding risk, demonstrating particular value for high-bleeding-risk populations. Future multicenter RCTs are warranted to validate applicability of NM in non-East Asian populations.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261399024, identifier: PROSPERO CRD420251077578.

records.title: Safeguarding biomedical AI: a critical scoping review of privacy-enhancing technologies, hybrid approaches, and deployment models.

content.title: Safeguarding biomedical AI: a critical scoping review of privacy-enhancing technologies, hybrid approaches, and deployment models.
content.abstract:
Background

Biomedical artificial intelligence (AI) requires the integration of privacy-enhancing technologies (PETs) to safeguard sensitive clinical, imaging, and genomic data while preserving analytical utility.

Objectives

This review critically and systematically maps applications of PETs across the biomedical AI lifecycle in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines and evaluates their technical trade-offs, deployment feasibility, and residual risks.

Methods

We systematically searched PubMed, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and Scopus for studies published between 2015 and 2025. Eligible studies addressed differential privacy, federated learning, secure multiparty computation, homomorphic encryption, or hybrid approaches in biomedical AI. Data were charted on PET type, modality, lifecycle stage, utility metrics, privacy parameters, and deployment considerations. A critical appraisal rubric assessed threat-model adequacy, methodological clarity, reproducibility, privacy-utility transparency, and deployment realism. Additionally, we hand-searched major venues (USENIX Security, NeurIPS, AAAI) and screened Google Scholar for grey literature, applying de-duplication across sources.

Results

We identified 87 studies spanning clinical decision support, genomics, and medical imaging. From 25,761 initial records, 3,754 underwent title/abstract screening and 1,968 underwent full-text assessment. PETs demonstrated distinct strengths and limitations: differential privacy provided provable guarantees but reduced performance on imbalanced data; federated learning improved data access but remained vulnerable to gradient leakage; and cryptographic methods ensured confidentiality at high computational cost. Synthetic data generation supported privacy-conscious data sharing and benchmarking but remained sensitive to disclosure risk, fidelity loss, and subgroup representation. Hybrid and emerging approaches, including trusted execution environments, zero-knowledge proofs, and privacy-preserving transformer architectures, mitigated composability gaps yet lacked full end-to-end assurance. Case studies at hospital and biobank scale illustrated practical feasibility and infrastructure demands.

Conclusions

Situating PETs within technical and operational contexts clarifies their capabilities, limitations, and deployment challenges. Residual risks persist, including fairness concerns, inference-time leakage, and overreliance on PETs as compliance proxies. Sustained technical innovation and institutional governance remain essential for the trustworthy integration of PETs in biomedical AI.

records.title: Mobile pharmacovigilance: a comprehensive review.

content.title: Mobile pharmacovigilance: a comprehensive review.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Adverse drug reactions (ADRs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) remain major contributors to morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs worldwide, while spontaneous reporting systems continue to suffer from substantial underreporting and incomplete documentation. The rapid advancement of mobile health (mHealth) technologies has introduced mobile pharmacovigilance as an innovative approach to improve the efficiency, accessibility, and quality of ADR reporting. This review aims to comprehensively evaluate the role of mobile applications in pharmacovigilance, with particular emphasis on ADR and SAE reporting, regulatory integration, user engagement, and future technological developments.

Methods

A hybrid systematic-narrative review methodology was adopted using PRISMA-guided literature identification across PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Google Scholar, and grey literature from the World Health Organization (WHO), regulatory agencies, and pharmacovigilance organizations. The review synthesizes evidence from studies evaluating mobile-based pharmacovigilance platforms, including WEB-RADR, Med Safety App, MedWatcher, My eReport France, VigiBIP, and V-safe.

Results

The findings demonstrate that mobile applications significantly improve both the quantity and quality of ADR reports by reducing reporting time, minimizing missing data, and enhancing report completeness through standardized digital reporting forms. Furthermore, mobile platforms have strengthened patient participation, enabled real-time safety surveillance during public health emergencies such as the COVID-19 pandemic, and facilitated bidirectional communication between healthcare professionals, patients, and regulatory authorities. Despite these advantages, challenges including digital inequality, limited regulatory harmonization, privacy concerns, low awareness, and inconsistent integration with national pharmacovigilance systems continue to hinder widespread adoption.

Conclusion

Emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, electronic health record integration, blockchain, and advanced data analytics are expected to further transform mobile pharmacovigilance. Overall, mobile applications represent a promising strategy for strengthening global pharmacovigilance systems by enabling timely, accurate, patient-centered, and efficient drug safety monitoring.

records.title: Deep learning-based radiomics and pathomics for decoding tumor microenvironment and predicting immunotherapy outcomes in gastric cancer.

content.title: Deep learning-based radiomics and pathomics for decoding tumor microenvironment and predicting immunotherapy outcomes in gastric cancer.
content.abstract: Although immune checkpoint inhibitors have reshaped the therapeutic landscape of gastric cancer, durable responses are achieved in only a minority of patients. The tumor microenvironment, particularly immune-cell composition and spatial organization, critically modulates cancer progression and the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Nevertheless, the lack of clinically accessible approaches for spatially resolving the tumor immune contexture, whether by direct pathological quantification or indirect radiomic inference, has hindered a mechanistic understanding of how it dictates immunotherapy outcomes. Deep learning-based radiomics and pathomics extract high-dimensional phenotypic information from radiological and pathological images, thereby characterizing tumors at macroscopic and microscopic scales. Each modality, however, captures only a partial view of the tumor microenvironment. Multimodal models can integrate complementary imaging features associated with tumor heterogeneity and spatial immune organization, thus improving predictive performance and linking multimodal features to immune-related biological processes. In this review, we summarize recent advances in deep learning-based radiomics, pathomics, and multimodal frameworks for decoding the immune microenvironment and predicting immunotherapy outcomes in gastric cancer. We also discuss their potential to complement established biomarkers and support personalized treatment decisions. Finally, we highlight key challenges, including limited data availability, interinstitutional variability, insufficient external validation, poor interpretability, and barriers to clinical implementation. Addressing these limitations may accelerate the development of robust imaging biomarkers for guiding immunotherapy decisions in gastric cancer.

records.title: Effects of different electrical stimulation on depression: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

content.title: Effects of different electrical stimulation on depression: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Depression is a prevalent psychiatric disorder characterised by persistent low mood and anhedonia, substantially impairing quality of life. Conventional treatments show variable efficacy and tolerability, with high post-discontinuation relapse rates. Electrical stimulation has emerged as an alternative intervention, but comparative efficacy and safety of different modalities remain uncertain. This systematic review and network meta-analysis aimed to synthesise evidence and quantitatively compare electrical stimulation approaches for depression.

Methods

A systematic search of 13 databases was conducted for randomised controlled trials (RCTs) published from inception to 16 July 2026. Methodological quality and risk of bias were assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool, and certainty of evidence was evaluated with the GRADE framework. Frequentist network meta-analysis was performed using STATA 18.0. Publication bias was assessed via funnel plot inspection, and sensitivity analyses examined the robustness of findings.

Results

A total of 33 RCTs involving 2,664 participants and nine electrical stimulation modalities were included. Pairwise meta-analysis showed that electrical stimulation was associated with a significantly improved clinical response rate (OR = 2.78, 95% CI 1.50 to 5.16) and a reduction in depressive symptom severity (SMD = -0.90, 95% CI -1.27 to -0.54) among patients with depression, along with a favourable safety profile (OR = 0.88, 95% CI 0.52 to 1.49). However, therapeutic effects varied across modalities. Specifically, Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) ranked highest for improving the clinical response rate (SUCRA = 99.9%; OR = 4.12, 95% CI 3.08 to 5.16), whereas transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) ranked highest for reducing the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD) score (SUCRA = 71.3%; SMD = -1.70, 95% CI -2.80 to -0.60). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of these results.

Conclusions

Electrical stimulation is associated with improved clinical response rates and reduced depressive symptom severity in patients with depression, and is generally well tolerated. Among the modalities examined, taVNS demonstrated a relative advantage in improving clinical response, while tDCS showed a relative advantage in alleviating depressive symptom severity. However, given the low certainty of the evidence underpinning these findings, they require confirmation in larger, higher-quality randomised controlled trials.

Systematic review registration

[url], identifier CRD420251103264.

records.title: Application of artificial intelligence in paediatric oncology imaging.

content.title: Application of artificial intelligence in paediatric oncology imaging.
content.abstract: Paediatric oncology relies heavily on medical imaging for diagnosis, treatment planning, and longitudinal disease monitoring. Yet the field faces unique challenges, including a limited number of patients, diverse anatomy, motion artefacts, and a global shortage of subspecialised radiologists. These constraints can compromise diagnostic accuracy, prolong workflows, and increase the risk of errors, highlighting a critical need for innovative solutions. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative tool capable of enhancing the entire imaging pipeline. From acquisition to reporting, AI-driven methods show potential to improve image quality, correct motion artefacts, harmonise multicentre datasets, and accelerate scans while reducing radiation exposure. Deep learning models and radiomics have been shown capable of precise tumour segmentation, early lesion detection, and classification, while integration with clinical and molecular data supports individualised staging, prognosis, and therapeutic decision-making. Beyond analysis, natural language processing and large language models can streamline report generation and clinical documentation, potentially enabling more efficient communication and workflow optimisation. Despite these advances, paediatric applications remain constrained by small, heterogeneous datasets, limited paediatric-specific models, and challenges in generalisability, explainability, and regulatory approval. Strategies such as model generalisation across new datasets, the development of retrainable generic models, privacy-preserving training, and synthetic data generation can help overcome these barriers, thereby improving model robustness and promoting equity in care. By augmenting rather than replacing radiologists, AI holds the potential to transform paediatric oncology imaging, improving diagnostic precision, workflow efficiency, and enhancing access to high-quality care. Continued collaboration between clinicians, data scientists, and regulatory bodies will be essential to realise this promise safely and effectively.

records.title: The impact of self-modeling on athletic performance and self-efficacy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
records.publisher: Frontiers in sports and active living

content.title: The impact of self-modeling on athletic performance and self-efficacy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Self-modeling, as a pedagogical approach in physical education, can effectively promote students' acquisition of movement skills and enhance their self-efficacy. However, the efficacy of self-modeling interventions remains controversial, and there is currently no objective, comprehensive evidence demonstrating their effectiveness in physical education instruction.

Methods

This study systematically evaluates the effects of self-modeling as an observational learning intervention on athletic performance and self-efficacy, along with its operational conditions, through a systematic review and meta-analysis.

Results

Self-modeling yields moderate to large positive influences on athletic performance and significantly enhances self-efficacy to a moderate degree. One week after the intervention ended, however, the improvement in athletic performance did not persist. Regression analysis revealed that intervention dose was the primary factor influencing effectiveness, with larger doses yielding more pronounced effects. Age, exercise experience, skill classification, and control group intervention type did not demonstrate significant moderating effects.

Discussion

The use of self-modeling in physical education and competitive sports can effectively enhance athletic performance and self-efficacy. However, its effects are dose-dependent and exhibit limited short-term sustainability. Future research should further clarify optimal intervention protocols and long-term mechanisms.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?ID=CRD420261477126, PROSPERO CRD420261477126.

records.title: Integrating Transcriptomics and Metabolomics for Clinical Disease Detection: A Critical Review of Emerging Diagnostic Methodologies.

content.title: Integrating Transcriptomics and Metabolomics for Clinical Disease Detection: A Critical Review of Emerging Diagnostic Methodologies.
content.abstract: Transcriptomics and metabolomics occupy mechanistically complementary positions in the molecular hierarchy of disease: gene expression characterizes upstream regulatory dysregulation, while metabolomics captures the downstream biochemical consequence at the functional endpoint of that cascade. Applied alone, each yields only a partial view of complex, multifactorial disease. This critical review evaluates the workflows, platforms and computational strategies of both disciplines, appraising their diagnostic utility, translational limitations and clinical laboratory adaptability.We examine integration methodologies spanning correlation-based approaches, multiblock latent factor models, network-guided pathway fusion and machine-learning architectures, and set out the parameter sensitivity and reproducibility limitations that the applied literature systematically underreports. These methodological claims are then tested against published practice through two in-depth case studies, in sepsis and non-small cell lung cancer, selected as contrasting exemplars. Persistent barriers are identified and discussed: pre-analytical variability, the transcriptome-metabolome correlation gap (r ≈ 0.3-0.4), incomplete reference databases, the absent proteome layer, and the lack of standardized clinical validation frameworks. We further argue that the missing proteome layer is not only a mechanistic gap but a formal obstacle to causal inference from two-layer data.Emerging solutions, including deep-learning fusion, explainable artificial intelligence and foundation models, are assessed alongside their documented limitations. We report that no biomarker derived from integrated transcriptomic-metabolomic analysis has undergone analytical validation, entered regulatory qualification, or reached clinical implementation, and that where diagnostic performance is reported it belongs to a single-platform model rather than to the integrated signature. Harmonized workflows, standardized reporting and regulatory-grade validation remain prerequisites for clinical adoption.

records.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Orthognathic Surgery: A Scoping Review.

content.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Orthognathic Surgery: A Scoping Review.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) has gained growing interest in the field of orthognathic surgery due to its potential to improve diagnostic accuracy, surgical planning, and treatment outcomes. This scoping review maps literature from 2017 to May 2025 to identify AI applications in orthognathic surgery, assess their clinical relevance, and discuss the associated ethical, legal, and technical limitations. Methods: This scoping review further examines the stages of the orthognathic surgical workflow at which AI applications have been prospectively validated, the artificial intelligence methodologies applied to virtual surgical planning and outcome prediction, and the main methodological, ethical, and legal factors that may constrain broader clinical adoption. Results: A total of 62 studies were included, covering AI use in cephalometric analysis, virtual surgical planning (VSP), outcome prediction, and intraoperative support. While AI demonstrates remarkable potential in orthognathic planning, current approaches are often limited by heterogeneous methodologies and retrospective validation. Conclusions: Future studies should prioritize prospective, multicentre designs integrating AI-assisted decision-making directly into the clinical workflow, with emphasis on model interpretability, patient-specific accuracy, and ethical transparency. These questions extend beyond mapping applications by emphasizing clinical validation, methodological rigor, and ethical accountability-dimensions insufficiently explored in prior reviews.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Pediatric Cardiovascular Genetics: From Multimodal Diagnosis to Risk Prediction and Precision Therapeutics.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Pediatric Cardiovascular Genetics: From Multimodal Diagnosis to Risk Prediction and Precision Therapeutics.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored as a bridge between high-dimensional cardiovascular phenotyping and genomic interpretation in children with inherited and congenital heart disease. This review focuses specifically on where AI-assisted approaches in pediatric cardiovascular genetics have progressed beyond proof-of-concept, how the maturity of evidence differs between general genomic tools and pediatric cardiovascular applications, and what is required for responsible clinical translation. Inherited and rare cardiovascular disorders are characterized by genetic heterogeneity, incomplete penetrance, variable expressivity, and age-dependent phenotypes, while modern sequencing, imaging, and longitudinal monitoring generate data that are difficult to integrate using conventional approaches alone. AI-assisted methods are being investigated across diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic domains, including computational phenotyping, genomic variant prioritization, electrocardiographic and imaging analysis, multimodal risk prediction, and selection of candidates for precision therapies. The strongest pediatric cardiovascular evidence currently comes from externally evaluated ECG and echocardiographic models and from large outcome-prediction cohorts, whereas many genomic tools-including variant callers and pathogenicity predictors-remain general-purpose methods that have not been specifically validated in pediatric cardiovascular genetics. Recent disease-specific genomic models and automated reanalysis frameworks illustrate a shift toward more clinically contextualized interpretation, but current evidence remains limited by retrospective design, small or selectively assembled rare-disease cohorts, domain shift, population bias, incomplete calibration, and uncertain clinical utility. Accordingly, AI should be viewed as a governed decision-support layer rather than an autonomous authority. With external validation, transparent reporting, longitudinal monitoring, and multidisciplinary oversight, AI has the potential to augment specialist expertise and may support earlier diagnosis, improved risk stratification, and more individualized treatment.

records.title: Effects of mind-body exercise on motor function, quality of life, and depressive symptoms in patients with Parkinson's disease: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

content.title: Effects of mind-body exercise on motor function, quality of life, and depressive symptoms in patients with Parkinson's disease: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

This study used network meta-analysis to compare and rank the effects of different mind-body exercises on motor function, depression, and quality of life in patients with Parkinson's disease, to inform clinical practice.

Methods

PubMed, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Embase, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang Database, and VIP Database were searched from inception to June 8, 2026, for randomized controlled trials of mind-body exercise interventions in Parkinson's disease. Network meta-analysis was performed using Stata version 18.0. Direct and indirect evidence was synthesized, and interventions were ranked using the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA). Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool and the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach, respectively.

Results

A total of 43 studies involving 2,337 patients with Parkinson's disease were included. For balance measured using the Berg Balance Scale, dance was significantly more effective than no treatment, walking, and usual care. For functional mobility measured using the Timed Up and Go Test, qigong was significantly more effective than tai chi, Dance, stretching, no treatment, and usual care. For overall motor function measured using the Unifed Parkinson's Disease rating Scale, Part III, yoga was significantly more effective than usual care and no treatment. For depressive symptoms measured using the Hamilton Depression Scale, tai chi was significantly more effective than qigong, no treatment, walking, and usual care. For health-related quality of life, as measured by the Parkinson's Disease Questionnaire, qigong was significantly more effective than usual care.

Conclusion

Moderate-certainty evidence supported benefits of dance for balance and qigong for functional mobility and quality of life compared with usual care, but superiority over other exercise modalities remains uncertain. For overall motor function, the current evidence is insufficient to identify a clearly superior mind-body exercise intervention, and the findings for Pilates and yoga remain uncertain, with the significant effects of yoga not proving robust in sensitivity analysis. Tai chi showed potential benefits for depressive symptoms; however, this finding should be interpreted cautiously because it was based on a limited number of studies and relied substantially on indirect comparisons.

Systematic review registration

PROSPERO, CRD420261418269.

records.title: Empowerment or dependency? A systematic review of the impacts of intelligent assessment and generative AI on learners' self-beliefs and cognitive agency in music education.

content.title: Empowerment or dependency? A systematic review of the impacts of intelligent assessment and generative AI on learners' self-beliefs and cognitive agency in music education.
content.abstract: Although artificial intelligence is fundamentally reshaping the ecology of music learning, existing research has disproportionately emphasized performance outcomes while underexamining psychological mechanisms, leaving the tension between technological empowerment and cognitive dependence theoretically underarticulated. Following PRISMA 2020, we systematically searched four databases and included 21 empirical studies to examine how three AI tool types-assessment-oriented AI, generative AI, and Comprehensive/adaptive AI-differentially shape learners' self-beliefs and cognitive agency in music education. The evidence base remains geographically and developmentally concentrated: most studies were conducted in China and in higher education, while early childhood settings were absent. Using thematic analysis, we conducted cross-type comparisons and synthesized psychological pathways. Assessment-oriented AI most consistently strengthened ability beliefs via objectified, visualized feedback and positioned cognitive agency around self-monitoring, self-reactiveness, and self-reflectiveness. Generative AI tended to enhance value-attitude beliefs and intentionality by lowering technical barriers and reconfiguring learners' creative roles toward aesthetic decision-making and output curation. Comprehensive/Adaptive AI more often supported forethought and sustained engagement by dynamically maintaining alignment between task challenge and learner capability. Across studies, psychological empowerment manifested as increased perceived competence and control, heightened motivation and engagement, and visible self-regulated learning behaviors. Cognitive dependence, however, emerged through outsourcing evaluative authority, score-driven goal distortion, algorithm-accommodating self-censorship, and attributional shifts that tether confidence to technological support. Developmental differences were also observed regarding dependence mechanisms: primary learners tended to perceive AI as a restrictive "scoring referee," whereas higher education students demonstrated strategic agency in orchestrating AI assistance. Specifically, a critical construct-tool mismatch was identified: while assessment AI consistently supports self-reflectiveness, generative AI currently lacks sufficient evidence for fostering learners' forethought. In light of the identified construct-tool mismatch, future research should prioritize addressing the paucity of evidence on how generative and adaptive AI foster forethought and intentionality, thereby clarifying whether such technologies ultimately reconstruct or erode learners' cognitive agency.

records.title: Impact of artificial intelligence on electronic health record-related burnouts among healthcare professionals: systematic review.

content.title: Impact of artificial intelligence on electronic health record-related burnouts among healthcare professionals: systematic review.
content.abstract:
Introduction

The implementation of electronic health records (EHRs) has revolutionized modern clinical practice, increasing efficiency, accessibility, and quality of care. Nevertheless, EHR-related workload has been considered as a significant contributor to healthcare professionals' burnout, a syndrome associated with emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and reduced personal accomplishment. As modern health system explores technological solutions, artificial intelligence (AI) has gained attention for its potential to facilitate documentation processes and alleviate cognitive burden. This systematic review aims to explore and understand the impact of artificial intelligence on burnout associated with electronic health records among healthcare professionals.

Methods

A systematic literature review was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Relevant studies published between 2019 and 2025 were retrieved from three electronic databases: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science. The search strategy included three main domains: artificial intelligence, electronic health records, and healthcare professional burnout. Eligible included studies are peer-reviewed original research articles that evaluated the impact of AI-based technologies on burnout among healthcare professionals. The screening and selection processes were carried out by following the PRISMA framework. Methodological quality assessment of the included studies was performed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Tools.

Results

Of the 287 records initially identified, eight studies met the inclusion criteria. The majority of identified studies were conducted in the United States and Canada.
